chapter: Reel 4: boyhood bands and the drummers he admired
title: Lettego, cousin Harold and the first drummer who inspired him
summary: He recalls a Bahamian drummer nicknamed Lettego, with a megaphone on the snare, at his father's bootleg parties, and his father's opposition to music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Panama, you talked about drumming and when you started drumming -- were there any drummers that you heard that inspired you to want to be a drummer? I know in my case, I used to hear Duke's band come through and admired Braud Hat Brow and I thought he was a marvelous base player and I wanted to be like him. But was there anybody, any drummers that you looked up to?

Well, there was a guy in Miami, his last name was Abrista, but one night a couple of guys got in a fight, and he was from the Bahamas and he was telling the guys to let him go, but instead of saying let him go, he said, "lette go", and he got this nickname, "Lettego", and everybody used to call him Lettego and so he and my cousin Harold who was a trumpet player, and he used to play all the house parties around Miami.

And my father was a bootlegger, and like every one once a month, he would have a party at the house so he could sell his liquor, and my cousin Harold and Lettego and a banjo player named Birdie and a base player named Fletcher, they all used to play all the house parties around there.
In fact, that's when I first saw a Coca Cola bottle being used as a mute. I think I was about 6 or 7 years old at the time, but I remember it well.

And I saw him playing the drums, and he was singing, which I can't do -- but he was singing, and he also would take the megaphone and put it on the snare drum and would blow through it and he got a crazy jazz sound out of this drum with the megaphone. And that's when I decided that was for me.

Although, like my father, my father had -- he did not want me to be a musician; he was deadly against me being a musician, because my cousin Harold and Lettego and them, all they would do was sit up there and drink all night and sleep all day, and spend all the money they made -- and Daddy just thought that was not the kind of life for me, although I wish he had lived to see what happened and the end result, as far as my being a musician, because I think he would have been pretty proud to have seen what happened to me. But he passed away before all this materialized.
